assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I heard you might change the cell phone policy at our school. I think you should go with Policy 1, the one where we can bring our phones and use them at lunch and free time but they have to be off in class. Here is why I think that.

First, kids need phones to talk to their parents. A lot of us don't go straight home after school. I have practice until five some days and my mom's work hours change every week, so she doesn't always know when she can pick me up. If practice gets cancelled or my ride can't come I have to tell her somehow. I know there is a phone in the office but its only one phone and there are hundreds of kids here. Parents want to reach us too. If you ban phones we would still have to figure all that out, it would just be way harder.

Second, I don't think Policy 2 would even work. Phones are small. Kids who want them are going to hide them in a pocket or in their locker. Then teachers have to spend time looking for phones and taking them away and arguing with kids, when they could be teaching. Also if almost everybody is breaking a rule then kids start to think rules don't really matter. Policy 1 is fair so most kids will follow it. Then teachers only have to deal with the few kids who don't.

Another reason is Policy 1 still keeps phones out of class. The whole problem with phones is they distract people during lessons. Both policies stop that. With Policy 1 if a teacher sees your phone or hears it in class they can take it till the end of the day. Nobody wants that because then you don't have it at lunch.

My last reason is we need to learn when to put our phones away on our own. When we get jobs or go to college nobody is going to lock up our phones for us. We will just have to know to turn it off in a meeting and check it on a break. With Policy 1 we can practice that now, while there are still teachers around to tell us when we mess up. I think that is better than never learning it.

I know you want students to pay attention in class and I want that too. Policy 1 does that without taking away something our families really need. Please think about it before you decide.

Sincerely,
A student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I heard that you are thinking about changing the cell phone policy. I am writing to ask you to pick Policy 1. Students could bring phones and use them at lunch and during free time, and the phones would stay off in class.

My first reason is about getting home. A lot of us do not go straight home after school. I have practice until five on some days, and my mom works a shift that changes every week. If practice gets cancelled or my ride does not show up, I have to tell her somehow. The office has a phone, but it is one line for a few hundred kids. Parents also call us to say when plans change. A total ban would not make that go away. It would be unsafe and scary for kids who walk or wait outside alone, and it would not be fair to worried parents.

My second reason is that Policy 2 would be hard to enforce. Phones are small. Kids who want them will keep them in a pocket or a locker. Teachers would have to search and take phones and argue, and that is a waste of a class period. Most kids would break the rule anyway, and then the rule is just a joke. Policy 1 asks for less, and teachers would only have to deal with the few who do not listen.

Third, Policy 1 still covers class time. The problem with phones is that they distract people during lessons, and both policies deal with that. Under Policy 1 a phone that is seen or heard in class can be taken until the end of the day. Kids would not want to lose it, so they would keep it put away.

Fourth, we are going to have to learn this at some point. At a job or in college nobody is going to lock up our phones for us. We will have to turn them off in a meeting and check them on a break. I do not think a ban teaches that. It just hides the thing for a few years.

I know you want students to pay attention in class, and I want that too. Policy 2 sounds strict, but Policy 1 is the better and fairer choice. It gives you quiet classrooms, and it lets families trust that they can reach us when they need to. I hope you will choose it. Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A student
